To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a single dose of 20 mg letrozole, administered at the time of follicular diameter of 12 mm, 18 mm, or after ovulation, did not induce dominant-follicle regression or failure to form a corpus luteum, but did cause suppression of estradiols and an increase in FSH and LH levels.

a single dose of letrozoles administered to women in the early follicular phase of the menstrual cycle did not prevent the growth of the dominant follicle or its ovulation, but did suppress estradiol synthesis and stimulate the release of FSH and lH from the pituitary gland.

the administration of a single dose 20 mg letrozole at the time of follicle selection (12 mm or 18 mm) or post ovulation (first day of the luteal phase) does not affect the dominant follicle growth rate, peak diameter or the inter-ovulatory cycle interval.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the treatment of ovarian dysfunction.
the impact of a brief, one-time exposure to an aromatase inhibiting agent, letrozole, on follicular development and ovulation in healthy, normally cycling, premenopausal women.
the development and application of novel methods for the analysis of data from longitudinal studies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

administration of a single 2.0 mg dose of letrozol at the times of follicle selection (when the diameter is 12 mm) or post-ovulation (the day following ovulation) is not detrimental to follicular development, ovulation, or corpus luteum function.
the single administration of letrozole at the time of dominant follicle selection (at a dose of 20 mg) did not induce dominant ovarian follicle regression or luteal failure.

a single dose of Letrozol (20 mg) administered at the time of the follicle reaching a diameter of 18mm did not induce dominant follice regression and was not detrimental to subsequent follicle growth and ovulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a single dose of letrozol at the time of dominant follicle selection does not affect follicular development, luteal formation, or the emergence of a new follicle wave.

a single 20mg dose of an aromastase inhibitor (letrozoole) administered at the defined times of follicular phase (12mm and 18mm) or post-ovulation (first day of luteal phase) did not induce dominant folllicle regression or failure in the formation of corpus lutea.

the administration of a single dose (20 mg) of letrozole to women with regular cycles and no known fertility problems does not appear to affect the development of the dominant follicle, the timing of ovulation or the ability to produce a corpus luteum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single dose of 20 mg of Letrozole does not appear to negatively impact the ovulatory process.
a single dose of letrozol can be used to suppress the estradiol surge in a dominant follicle without compromising follicle selection or ovulation.
it is safe to give a single 20mg dose of an aromastase inhibitor (letrozoole) to women in the follicular phase.
